from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Vectors are directed segments in 2D space.",
            "They represent magnitude and specific direction.",
            "Think of them as instructions for movement."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("What is a Vector? (Visualizing Movement)", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create a 2D arrow representing a vector from origin #FFD700
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 5], y_range=[0, 5], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'D4', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        vector = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(3, 2), color="#FFD700")
        self.add(vector)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show vector movement animation with trail #FFFFFF
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        trail = TracedPath(vector.get_end, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        self.add(trail)
        self.play(Create(vector), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight vector components X and Y #FF4500
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        
        x_line = DashedLine(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(3, 0), color="#FF4500")
        y_line = DashedLine(axes.c2p(3, 0), axes.c2p(3, 2), color="#FF4500")
        
        x_label = MathTex("x=3", color="#FF4500", font_size=24)
        y_label = MathTex("y=2", color="#FF4500", font_size=24)
        
        self.place_at_grid(x_label, 'F4')
        x_label.next_to(x_line, DOWN)
        
        self.place_at_grid(y_label, 'D6')
        y_label.next_to(y_line, RIGHT)
        
        self.play(Create(x_line), Write(x_label), Create(y_line), Write(y_label), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Scalar Multiplication: Stretching Space", [
            "Scalars stretch or shrink vectors.",
            "They change length, maintaining orientation.",
            "Negative scalars reverse the direction."
        ])
        
        # Setup vector
        vec_base = np.array([1, 1, 0])
        vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=vec_base, buff=0)
        self.place_at_grid(vec, 'C4')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        vec.set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Create(vec))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        new_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=vec_base * 2, buff=0).set_color("#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(new_vec, 'C4')
        self.play(Transform(vec, new_vec))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        neg_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=vec_base * -1, buff=0).set_color("#FF4500")
        self.place_at_grid(neg_vec, 'C4')
        self.play(Transform(vec, neg_vec))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Basis vectors i and j are building blocks.", "Any 2D vector is their linear combination.", "They define the coordinate grid."]
        self.setup_layout("Basis Vectors: The Building Blocks", lecture_lines)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 3], y_range=[-1, 3], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.6)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6")
        self.add(axes)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        i_hat = Vector(RIGHT, color="#00FFFF")
        j_hat = Vector(UP, color="#FFD700")
        
        # Placing at grid coordinates using axes.c2p
        i_vec = axes.c2p(1, 0)
        j_vec = axes.c2p(0, 1)
        origin = axes.c2p(0, 0)
        
        i_hat.shift(origin - i_hat.get_start())
        j_hat.shift(origin - j_hat.get_start())
        
        self.play(Create(i_hat))
        self.play(Create(j_hat))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF4500")
        
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v} = 3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}", color="#FF4500")
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, "A6")
        
        v_vector = Vector(axes.c2p(3, 2) - origin, color="#FF4500")
        v_vector.shift(origin - v_vector.get_start())
        
        self.play(Create(v_vector))
        self.play(Write(v_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        # Visual hint for grid
        grid_lines = NumberPlane(x_range=[-1, 3], y_range=[-1, 3]).scale(0.6).move_to(axes.get_center())
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_lines))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", ["Vectors combine instructions for spatial transformation.", "They form the basis for coordinate systems.", "Linear algebra enables complex visual movement."])
        
        # Create vectors
        vec1 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color=BLUE)
        vec2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color=GREEN)
        vec3 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1 + UP*1, color=RED)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(vec1, vec2, vec3))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Indicate(vec1), Indicate(vec2), Indicate(vec3))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(vec1, vec2, vec3))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra: Vectors as Spatial Guides

sections.title: What is a Vector? (Visualizing Movement)
sections.content: Introduce vectors as directed line segments in 2D space defined by magnitude and direction. Explain how a vector acts as an 'instruction' to move from an origin (0,0) to a coordinate (x,y).
sections.example: Visualize a robotic turtle starting at the origin; a vector [3, 2] is the specific command for it to walk 3 units right and 2 units up.

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Head-to-Tail Rule
sections.content: Demonstrate that adding vectors corresponds to sequential movements. Graphically, this is shown by placing the tail of the second vector at the head of the first.
sections.example: The turtle walks [3, 2] (first vector), then walks [1, 4] (second vector). The 'resultant' vector is the straight path from the origin to the turtle's final position [4, 6].

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication: Stretching Space
sections.content: Explain how multiplying a vector by a scalar (number) changes its length but keeps its orientation (unless negative). This 'stretches' or 'shrinks' the vector graphically.
sections.example: If a bird is flying along vector [1, 1], multiplying by 2 results in [2, 2], visually doubling the length of the flight path while maintaining the same diagonal angle.

sections.title: Basis Vectors: The Building Blocks
sections.content: Define 'i' [1, 0] and 'j' [0, 1] as the unit basis vectors. Explain that any 2D vector is simply a linear combination: x*i + y*j.
sections.example: Think of [3, 2] as a recipe: 3 portions of 'horizontal unit move' plus 2 portions of 'vertical unit move'. This shows why these two vectors are the 'grid' for all 2D space.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Recap that linear algebra is the study of how these spatial instructions combine to transform the entire grid, setting the stage for matrices and transformations.
sections.example: Summarize how simple vectors (arrows) form the coordinate system used in every video game to animate characters moving across a screen.
